audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Gwen Levels 2-3 and Skill at 4-5 and 6, while the prose says 'Levels 1-3 belong to Swain' and 'This is where it flips' at 6.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Swain/Skill/Skill/Gwen/Gwen/Gwen/Gwen and matches the prose.
Swain's only spike is Levels 1-3 poke; Gwen's are Level 6 Hallowed Mist and Riftmaker into his HP-stacking drain build.
audit.corrected: Each phase why names the ability and its cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were never stated.
audit.why: Riot on Nevermove: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the RETURN trip — the outgoing wave does nothing, so standing still once it has passed is the mistake. Riot on Demonic Ascension: 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions' — so Hallowed Mist, which only lets enemies inside it target Gwen, makes his ultimate expire rather than merely dodging it. Riot on Death's Hand: 'Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by', so the edge of the volley is far cheaper than the middle.
audit.corrected: Return-trip root, the ultimate's drain condition, and the bolt-stacking all written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tracked Demonic Ascension (120s) as the matchup-defining cooldown; the punishable one is Nevermove.
audit.why: Nevermove is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and is his only lock-down; it is also on a shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension.
audit.corrected: Nevermove is now the tracked cooldown, with its 10-12s gap as the trade window.

edits.before: Stack snips on the wave and tag him with the true-damage center. Identify how Swain contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are his. Death's Hand pierces from 750 and each extra bolt that hits adds damage — stand at the edge of the volley, not in it.

edits.before: E dash-attack-speed makes the snip window real. Only take the trade when Swain's Demonic Ascension is down.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on its RETURN trip, not on the way out — keep moving the moment the wave has passed you.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Swain must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Skip 'n Slash gives a reset, but with no Mist a landed Nevermove is still a free Death's Hand volley. Trade in its 10-12s gap.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Demonic Ascension's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your window opens: A Thousand Cuts out-sustains his chip, and anti-heal starts cutting the Soul Fragments that grow his bar permanently.

edits.before: Needles ramp the longer the fight goes — extended brawls are yours. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Swain's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension lasts only while he drains a champion — go untargetable inside Hallowed Mist and the form simply expires on him.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Demonic Ascension's cooldown.
edits.after: Riftmaker is your spike — his HP-stacking drain build is exactly what %-max-HP snips eat.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Swain carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on, extended Mist brawls are yours. Only Nevermove flips it, so never facecheck brush where the return wave can pin you.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Burst him before it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove (10-12s): it roots on the RETURN trip, so keep moving after the wave passes you. - Demonic Ascension (120s): it lasts only while he is draining a champion. - Needlework: kill windows only.

edits.before: Good trade: Stack passive on minions, E onto Swain with the center-Q ready, snip the %HP true damage, and W if he turns. Great trade: Swain wastes Demonic Ascension — commit the full pattern immediately. Bad trade: Dropping W early or fighting outside it against his key tool — the mist IS the matchup for ranged answers.
edits.after: Good trade: Stack passive on minions, E onto Swain with the center-Q ready, snip the %HP true damage, and W if he turns. Great trade: Nevermove's return wave whiffs — he has no root for 10-12s, so commit the full pattern. Bad trade: standing in the middle of Death's Hand, where every extra bolt that lands raises the damage.

edits.before: His drain. Burst him before it. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.before: That is Swain's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.

edits.before: Dropping W early or fighting outside it against his key tool — the mist IS the matchup for ranged answers.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. Burst him before it. When it is down — Snip him in your mist.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the return trip; Demonic Ascension expires unless he is draining a champion.

edits.before: W-mist his E — build MR and Snip before his R drain ramps. Gwen wins by trading around Swain's Demonic Ascension and cashing the pattern: build MR, W his root, and Snip fast.
edits.after: Dodge the return half of Nevermove, then out-brawl him: Demonic Ascension expires unless he keeps draining a champion, and Hallowed Mist puts you out of his reach.

edits.before: Hallowed Mist nullifies his Demonic Ascension all-in — its drain is AOE, so you snip untargetable while his R heals off minions instead of you.
edits.after: Hallowed Mist nullifies Demonic Ascension — the form lasts only while he drains a champion, so untargetable inside the fog you make his ultimate expire.

edits.before: Sidestep his Nevermove (E) — it travels slowly, so don't last-hit with minions stacked behind you where the root is easy to land
edits.after: Sidestep Nevermove (E) on its RETURN trip — the outgoing wave does not root, so keep moving the moment it passes you

notes: Nevermove rooting on the return wave and Demonic Ascension expiring without a champion to drain are the two facts that decide this lane; neither was on the page. Death's Hand also scales with how many of its bolts hit you, which makes the edge of the volley materially cheaper than the middle.
